+# QA script: bug-002 / N1, a fresh clone F5s straight into Docket
+
+Rule ID: DATA-1. The acceptance lines for N1 in `docs/plans/active/bug-002.dag.yaml` are the contract. They trace
+back to inv-009 #1 (I1), I4, #12 (I17) and I5.
+Branch: bug/bug-002/N1   Worktree: .claude/worktrees/bug-002-N1
+Commit under test: 4ebe53f or later. The work landed in 6ee2e95 (red), 35122e4 (green) and 9972c24 (the A1/I1 test
+fix). Record the SHA you test in the sign-off.
+Ports: the **API and web** profile's fixed ports. The API is on 5080 and the dev server, or preview, is on 4170.
+
+The Actual and Pass/Fail columns are empty. I wrote these steps from the files at 4ebe53f and haven't run them
+(note 4).
+
+## Preconditions
+
+- [ ] Visual Studio 2022 or later with the **Node.js development** workload, the .NET 10 SDK, and Node on `PATH`.
+- [ ] Nothing is listening on 5080 or 4170. Stop any API, dev server or preview started from a worktree.
+- [ ] Two PowerShell windows. **Shell 1** runs the commands. **Shell 2** runs only the poller (command P1, below).
+- [ ] Every step names its directory. "clone web" means `$env:TEMP\n1-fresh\src\Uinsure.Policies.Web`.
+
+## Commands the steps use
+
+P1, the poller. Run it in Shell 2 from any directory. It asks for `/trace.json` every 100 ms and prints the status and
+the first 60 characters of the body. `000` means the port refused the connection. It stops at the first 200, or after
+a minute.
+
+```powershell
+$f = "$env:TEMP\n1-trace.txt"; Remove-Item $f -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
+for ($i = 0; $i -lt 600; $i++) {
+  $c = curl.exe -s -o $f -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:4170/trace.json
+  $b = [string](Get-Content $f -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
+  "$c $($b.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(60, $b.Length)))"
+  if ($c -eq '200') { break }
+  Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 100
+}
+```
+
+P2 reads a compiled trail's stamp. Run it in Shell 1 from clone web, with `<file>` set to `public\trace.json` or
+`dist\trace.json`.
+
+```powershell
+(Get-Content <file> -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).compiledAt | Format-List sha, utc
+```
+
+## Steps
+
+### Part A: a clone with no node_modules (acceptance 1; inv-009 #1, I1)
+
+| # | Rule | Where | Action | Expected | Actual | Pass/Fail |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | DATA-1 | Shell 1, worktree root | `git clone --branch bug/bug-002/N1 . "$env:TEMP\n1-fresh"`, then `cd "$env:TEMP\n1-fresh\src\Uinsure.Policies.Web"; Test-Path node_modules; Test-Path public\trace.json` | The clone succeeds. Both `Test-Path` calls print `False`, because a fresh clone has neither (`public/` is git-ignored). Don't run `npm ci` yet | | |
+| 2 | DATA-1 | Shell 1, clone web | `node scripts/dev.mjs --port 4170 --strictPort; $LASTEXITCODE`. This is the program the F5 target `Vite dev server` runs (`.vscode/launch.json`) | It prints one line, ``Packages are not restored. Run `npm ci` in src/Uinsure.Policies.Web, then start again.``, and `$LASTEXITCODE` is `1`. There is no `Cannot find module` and no stack trace. Nothing listens on 4170 | | |
+| 3 | DATA-1 | Visual Studio, clone | Open `$env:TEMP\n1-fresh\Uinsure.Policies.slnx`. Choose the **API and web** profile and press F5 before any restore. Then Shift+F5 | The API starts, and `http://localhost:5080/health/live` answers healthy. The web target does one of two things (note 1). Either its debug console prints the line from step 2 and the target ends, with no `Cannot find module`. Or Visual Studio restores the packages itself on open (an `npm` entry in the Output window) and Vite starts as in step 8. Write down which happened | | |
+| 4 | DATA-1 | Shell 1, clone web | `node --version; npm ci; $LASTEXITCODE` | `npm ci` exits 0. If `node --version` is below `v22.22.0`, npm also prints an `EBADENGINE` warning that names `node: '>=22.22.0'` (step 12). It's a warning, not a refusal, because no `.npmrc` sets `engine-strict` | | |
+
+### Part B: the dev server answers while the trail compiles (acceptance 2; I4)
+
+| # | Rule | Where | Action | Expected | Actual | Pass/Fail |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 5 | DATA-1 | Shell 2 | Start P1 | It prints `000` lines. Nothing is listening yet | | |
+| 6 | DATA-1 | Shell 1, clone web | While P1 runs, `node scripts/dev.mjs --port 4170 --strictPort` | P1 changes from `000` to `503 The trail is compiling; try again in a moment.`, then stops at `200 {"schemaVersion":"1.0.0",…`. No 404 shows between them. Shell 1 prints `Local: http://localhost:4170/` only once the compile has ended, so after P1's first 503. If P1 jumps straight from `000` to `200`, the compile finished inside one 100 ms poll (note 2) | | |
+| 7 | DATA-1 | Shell 1, clone web | In a new tab, open `http://localhost:4170/`. Then run P2 on `public\trace.json`, `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --short` | The overview draws the trail, not "Could not load trace.json". P2's `sha` equals `git rev-parse HEAD`. `git status` doesn't list `public/`. Leave the dev server running | | |
+| 8 | DATA-1 | Visual Studio, clone | Stop the dev server in Shell 1 (Ctrl+C). In Visual Studio, F5 on **API and web** | The packages are restored now, so there's no "unable to launch" message. The API answers at `http://localhost:5080/health/live`. Docket opens at `http://localhost:4170/` in your default browser and draws the trail. Shift+F5 stops both, and nothing listens on 5080 or 4170 | | |

+### Part C: preview serves the built dist (acceptance 3; inv-009 #12, I17)
+

+| 10 | DATA-1 | Shell 1, clone web | `Remove-Item -Recurse public\trace.json, public\trace`, then `npm run preview -- --port 4170 --strictPort` | `Local: http://localhost:4170/` prints at once. No `trace compile` line prints, and no compile runs | | |
+| 11 | DATA-1 | Shell 2, then the browser | Run P1. Then open `http://localhost:4170/` | P1's first line is a `200` carrying the trail. Its body is `dist\trace.json`, so the `utc` matches step 9. The overview draws the trail | | |
+| 12 | DATA-1 | Shell 2, clone web | `Test-Path "$env:TEMP\n1-fresh\src\Uinsure.Policies.Web\public\trace.json"` | `False`. Preview served the built `dist/` and wrote nothing to `public/`. Stop preview with Ctrl+C in Shell 1 | | |
+
+### Part D: the Node minimum (acceptance 4; I5)
+
+| # | Rule | Where | Action | Expected | Actual | Pass/Fail |

+| 13 | DATA-1 | Shell 1, clone web | `Get-Content .nvmrc; (Get-Content package.json -Raw \| ConvertFrom-Json).engines.node` | `.nvmrc` holds `22.22.0` and `engines.node` is `>=22.22.0`, the same version. With nvm-windows, `nvm use (Get-Content .nvmrc)` switches to it | | |

+
+| # | Rule | Where | Action | Expected | Actual | Pass/Fail |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 14 | DATA-1 | Shell 1, worktree root | `npm --prefix src/Uinsure.Policies.Web run test -- -t "DATA-1 · "` | Every DATA-1 test passes, including the four in `unit/toolchain/data-1-first-run.test.ts` and the two in `unit/toolchain/data-1-trace-on-start.test.ts` (passed / failed / skipped: __ / __ / __) | | |
+
+## Covered by tests or gates, not by a step
+
+Run from the worktree root. The unit tests: `npm --prefix src/Uinsure.Policies.Web run test -- -t "DATA-1 · "`.
+
+| Rule | Test or gate | Why not a step |
+|---|---|---|
+| DATA-1 | `DATA-1 · a compile that fails is reported in the console, naming each problem, and no trace.json is served` (`unit/toolchain/data-1-trace-on-start.test.ts`) | Breaking the trail by hand isn't a QA action. While the compile is failing, `/trace.json` keeps answering 503 |
+| DATA-1 | `DATA-1 · the dev server answers on its port while the trail compiles…` (`unit/toolchain/data-1-first-run.test.ts`) | It runs on a trail with 300 extra commits, so the compile lasts long enough to catch the 503 every time. Step 6 might not catch it (note 2) |
+| DATA-1 | `DATA-1 · under vite preview a failed compile is reported…, or preview compiles nothing` (same file) | Steps 10 to 12 show the "compiles nothing" side. The failure side only runs if preview ever compiles again |
+| DATA-1 | "The reproduction test fails on the merge base and passes at the PR head" | The integrate gate (t9) and the PR's receipts show this, against merge base 6b6bdb5 |
+| DATA-1 | "The full suite and the rule-coverage check pass" | Gate t6 (done) and the post-rebase run at t9 |
+
+## Notes
+
+1. **Visual Studio might restore the packages before F5 gets the chance to fail.** The JavaScript project system can
+   run its own npm restore when it opens an `.esproj`. When it does, step 3 can't show the stop message, and step 2
+   is the proof. Either outcome meets the acceptance: the packages are restored, or the launch stops and names
+   `npm ci`. What fails is a `Cannot find module …vite.js`.
+2. **The 503 window can be short.** On the real trail the compile might finish in under a second. The poller only
+   sees the 503 if one of its asks lands inside that window. If it doesn't, run step 6 again. A straight
+   `000`→`200` still shows nothing broken, because the port never served a 404 or an older file. The unit test
+   lengthens the compile on purpose so it always catches the window.
+3. **The esproj's own `StartupCommand` still reads `npx vite --port 4170 --strictPort`.** F5 goes through the
+   `Vite dev server` configuration in `.vscode/launch.json`, which now runs `scripts/dev.mjs`, so steps 3 and 8 use
+   the guarded path. If you see the `npx vite` command run on a clone with no packages, write it as a defect against
+   step 3.
+4. **I haven't run these steps.** Visual Studio, the clone and the browser are outside what I run at the QA step. The
+   expected text comes from `scripts/dev.mjs`, `vite.config.ts`, `.vscode/launch.json`, `package.json` and `.nvmrc`
+   at 4ebe53f.
+5. Delete `$env:TEMP\n1-fresh` and `$env:TEMP\n1-trace.txt` when you're done.
